report.summary: Chunk 3 of 3 of daedalus/eval/mint.py: contains mint_task_from_landed_edit, mint_from_commit, confirm_task, load_minted_tasks, save_minted_tasks, add_minted_task, confirm_minted_task, and helper _log_mint_diagnostics.
risks: mint_task_from_landed_edit | medium | Uses report.get('wrote') which may be missing or empty; returns None. No validation on report shape. | Verify that offload.py always returns a dict with 'wrote' key.
mint_from_commit | medium | Uses _git to run diff-tree; no error handling if _git fails (returns None) or if _show fails. | Ensure _git and _show handle errors gracefully.
confirm_task | low | Mutates task dict in place; callers may not expect mutation. | Document mutation behavior or return a copy.
confirm_minted_task | low | Calls confirm_task which mutates task; then saves all tasks. If save fails, store may be inconsistent. | Add error handling for save failure.
add_minted_task | low | Overwrites task with same id; no versioning or conflict detection. | Consider adding timestamp or version field.
load_minted_tasks | low | Returns [] if file missing; but if file exists but corrupt, json.load may raise. | Add try/except for JSON decode error.

claims.text: A task that DID mint carries its own ``skipped_out_of_scope``/``must_include_dropped`` fields; this is what surfaces the same information -- and the no-task-minted ``reason`` -- for the cases where there is no task dict to carry it.
claims.why: The function checks diagnostics for 'skipped_out_of_scope' and 'reason' and logs them, handling cases where no task dict exists.

claims.text: ``report["wrote"]`` IS ``disk_changed`` from offload.py:194-197 -- the files that ACTUALLY changed on disk, found by diffing a before/after content-hash snapshot taken around the run.
claims.why: Cannot verify claim about offload.py internals; code not present.

claims.text: The model's self-reported ``files_changed`` is deliberately not read, for the same reason offload.py itself refuses to trust it for the write-mode gate.
claims.why: Cannot verify claim about offload.py behavior.

claims.text: The edit is assumed uncommitted (offload writes straight into the working tree and never commits): "before" is read from git HEAD, "after" from the file currently on disk.
A file the run created has no HEAD blob (before = None); a file it deleted has nothing left on disk (after = None).
claims.why: Code sets before = _show(...) which returns None if no blob; after = _read_worktree(...) which returns None if file missing.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` if there is nothing to mint: no writes reported, every write's content is symbol-identical to HEAD (e.g. a formatting-only touch this diff granularity can't see through), no written file is in the project's index scope, or only one in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists -- see the module docstring's CROSS-FILE ONLY rule).
claims.why: Cannot verify the CROSS-FILE ONLY rule or _mint_from_diffs behavior; code not in this chunk.

claims.text: Currently mints a single aggregate task per commit (via the same ``_mint_from_diffs`` used for landed edits); returns a list so a future split (e.g. one task per hunk, for very large commits) is additive rather than a signature change.
claims.why: Code returns [task] if task else [], a list.

claims.text: Returns ``[]`` for an unresolvable ref, a commit that touches no in-scope file, or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists) -- never raises.
claims.why: Cannot verify _mint_from_diffs behavior or cross-file rule.

claims.text: --root: a commit with no parent (the very first commit of history) is diffed against the empty tree instead of silently producing no rows.
claims.why: Code uses '--root' flag in diff-tree command.
Code increments confirmations and sets tier to 'primary' if threshold met.

claims.text: A no-op on a task that is not currently quarantined: a primary task doesn't need more confirming, and "confirming" a hand_reachable task is meaningless -- it was never gated in the first place.
Returns the same (mutated) dict for convenient chaining; callers that need the pre-mutation task should copy it first.
claims.why: Function returns the same task dict after mutation.

claims.text: This is the ONLY load path by which a minted task can reach ``daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks()`` and therefore any go/no-go number -- without it, ``mint_task_from_landed_edit``/``mint_from_commit`` produced dicts that lived only as long as the caller's local variable.
claims.why: Cannot verify claim about harness.all_tasks() usage.

claims.text: Sorted by id for deterministic iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent), matching the rest of this repo's output-determinism rule.
claims.why: Code returns sorted(data.get('tasks', []), key=lambda t: t['id']).

claims.text: Deterministic formatting (sorted keys, sorted by id) so the diff is meaningful in review -- same contract as ``harness.write_baseline``.
claims.why: Code sorts tasks by id and uses sort_keys=True in json.dump.

claims.text: Idempotent: minting the same diff twice (same target + same must_include, via the content hash in ``_mint_from_diffs``) yields the same id and overwrites in place rather than duplicating -- re-running a mint (e.g. after a rebase that reproduces an identical patch) must not inflate the quarantine count.
claims.why: Cannot verify _mint_from_diffs id generation; code uses by_id dict to deduplicate by id.

claims.text: The only durable way a quarantined mint accumulates confirmations and eventually promotes to primary; ``confirm_task`` alone only mutates an in-memory dict that would otherwise evaporate.
claims.why: Code loads tasks, calls confirm_task, saves, and returns the updated task.
